title: Thy Ways, O Lord, with Wise Design
description: Thy Ways, O Lord, with Wise Design in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 148 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Providence Mysterious”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy ways, O Lord, with wise de-sign, Are framed up-on thy throne a-bove, And ev-ery dark or bend-ing line Meets in the cen-tre of thy love.

lines: Thy ways, O Lord, with wise design,
Are framed upon thy throne above,
And every dark or bending line
Meets in the centre of thy love.
With feeble light, and half obscure,
Not knowing that the least are sure,
And the mysterious just and true.
They neither know nor trace the way;
But, trusting to thy piercing eye,
None of their feet to ruin stray,
Nor shall the weakest fail or die.
My favored soul shall meekly learn
To lay her reason at thy throne;
Too weak thy secrets to discern,
I'll trust thee for my guide alone.
